headline: UK Healthcare AI Regulations Fundamentally Broken, says industry report
summary: A new report reveals 7 in 10 stakeholders find existing UK AI healthcare regulations insufficient for safety and performance, with 6 in 10 citing data privacy issues. Over half call for a complete overhaul.
details: The UK's ambition for an "AI-enabled healthcare system" faces a major hurdle: its current AI regulations are fundamentally broken, according to a new industry report. Seven in ten stakeholders disagree that existing rules are sufficient for safety and performance.

The report, from the MHRA's National Commission on the Regulation of AI in Healthcare, gathered responses from 761 bodies. Six in ten respondents also found data privacy and governance regulations inadequate.

Currently, AI in UK healthcare is regulated under medical device regulations (MDR), lumping software with hardware. This framework struggles with AI's ability to drift, learn, and change behavior post-approval.
Post-market surveillance, crucial for monitoring AI systems after deployment, was deemed inadequate by 65% of respondents. There's no clear mechanism for handling AI performance changes over time.

Further gaps include insufficient transparency requirements (71% disagreement) and clinical evidence standards that don't account for AI's adaptive nature. Data governance frameworks were not designed with AI in mind.

Industry stakeholders, including AI health product builders, are calling for clearer responsibilities across the AI lifecycle. They seek comprehensive governance structures and proper training for healthcare professionals.

The constructive tone of the report is notable; the industry isn't avoiding regulation but is asking for a more suitable framework. Final recommendations from the National Commission are expected soon.
caption:
UK's ambition for "most AI-enabled healthcare system" is at risk. A new report reveals 70% of industry stakeholders say current AI regulations are "fundamentally broken" for safety and performance.

The UK's ambition for an "AI-enabled healthcare system" faces a major hurdle: its current AI regulations are fundamentally broken, according to a new industry report. Seven in ten stakeholders disagree that existing rules are sufficient for safety and performance.

The report, from the MHRA's National Commission on the Regulation of AI in Healthcare, gathered responses from 761 bodies. Six in ten respondents also found data privacy and governance regulations inadequate.

Currently, AI in UK healthcare is regulated under medical device regulations (MDR), lumping software with hardware. This framework struggles with AI's ability to drift, learn, and change behavior post-approval.

Post-market surveillance, crucial for monitoring AI systems after deployment, was deemed inadequate by 65% of respondents. There's no clear mechanism for handling AI performance changes over time.

Further gaps include insufficient transparency requirements (71% disagreement) and clinical evidence standards that don't account for AI's adaptive nature. Data governance frameworks were not designed with AI in mind.

Industry stakeholders, including AI health product builders, are calling for clearer responsibilities across the AI lifecycle. They seek comprehensive governance structures and proper training for healthcare professionals.

The constructive tone of the report is notable; the industry isn't avoiding regulation but is asking for a more suitable framework. Final recommendations from the National Commission are expected soon.
